order_note: No predecessor and no order on this engine. SQL 114 needs public.stakeholder_accounts with its is_active, is_primary, account_type, homeowner_name, homeowner_email and updated_at columns (restored Supabase schema) owned by checksops_admin and the roles checksops and authenticated. Settings > Stakeholder Accounts (src/components/disbursement/StakeholderAccountSettings.tsx) removes a non-payee stakeholder with UPDATE stakeholder_accounts SET is_active = false, is_primary = false and changes a stakeholder type with SET account_type (clearing homeowner_name and homeowner_email when it stops being a homeowner); on AWS those writes need a /data/write route (a later code PR, not part of this migration) and an UPDATE privilege for checksops on those columns, which no migration in this repository grants (the restored database gave checksops SELECT only, aws/db-copy/sql/02_grant_readonly_application_role.sql). The policy aws_write_stakeholder_accounts (aws/rls/sql/24_complete_write_policies.sql: FOR ALL TO authenticated, USING / WITH CHECK aws_can_write_tenant(tenant_id)) stays the authorization boundary. SQL 114 grants UPDATE (is_active, is_primary, account_type, homeowner_name, homeowner_email, updated_at) on stakeholder_accounts to checksops and authenticated and changes nothing else. If the read-only inspect finds both lines on all six columns already held it reports already_applied true and nothing is applied (the pin is then recorded as verified live, not applied). No later migration revokes these grants.
